pack.title: First dates
pack.description: Tests disguised as small talk. Answer the question, keep your dignity.

scenarios.setting: First date, over drinks. They ask about your income before you know each other well.
scenarios.jab: So anyway — how much do you make, roughly?

replies.line: I keep the number private. I'm happy to talk about my work.
replies.why: It protects financial details while offering a topic you welcome.
replies.delivery: Keep your expression relaxed and stress “private,” without accusing them of auditing you.

replies.why: It labels the timing as the problem, which lets the date continue cleanly.
replies.delivery: Say “Not a first-date question” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. ” without accusing them of auditing you.

replies.line: I'd rather keep the number private; what's something you enjoy about your work?
replies.why: It pairs a clear privacy preference with genuine curiosity.
replies.delivery: Keep your expression relaxed and stress “private,” without accusing them of auditing you.

replies.line: Somewhere between intern and Bond villain. You?
replies.why: A joke answer to an audit question signals the topic is closed and the night isn't.
replies.delivery: Keep “Somewhere between intern and Bond villain” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. ” without accusing them of auditing you.

trap.why: It adds contempt when a clear privacy boundary would express your decision.

scenarios.goal: Keep financial details private while continuing a date.

followUp.line: I prefer to keep the number private; I'm happy to talk about my work.
followUp.why: It sets a privacy boundary while offering a topic you welcome.
followUp.delivery: Keep your expression relaxed and stress “private,” without accusing them of auditing you.

scenarios.setting: First date. They've spent twenty minutes on their ex.
scenarios.jab: Sorry, sorry — my ex just really messed me up, you know?

replies.line: I hear you. Tonight I'm getting to know you, not them.
replies.why: It shows empathy while drawing the evening's boundary in one calm line.
replies.delivery: Start with warmth, pause, then make the redirect without rolling your eyes.

replies.line: Let's focus on tonight for a moment.
replies.why: It redirects attention to the current date without dismissing the past.
replies.delivery: Start with warmth, pause, then make the redirect without rolling your eyes.

replies.line: That sounds rough — I hope tonight can be a lighter chapter.
replies.why: Kindness about the hurt plus a gentle bid for the present keeps both intact.
replies.delivery: Start with warmth, pause, then make the redirect without rolling your eyes.

replies.line: Let's give tonight its own chapter.
replies.why: A gentle story metaphor invites attention to the present without ridiculing their hurt.
replies.delivery: Start with warmth, pause, then make the redirect without rolling your eyes.

followUp.jab: I can't help talking about them.
followUp.line: I hear it's still painful; I'd like us to spend some time in the present.
followUp.why: It acknowledges the hurt while naming the conversation you want.
followUp.delivery: Start with warmth, pause, then make the redirect without rolling your eyes.

scenarios.setting: End of a decent first date. They walk you to your car.

replies.line: Mine's not on the table tonight. I had a good time.
replies.why: It declines the invitation while acknowledging the evening without promising further contact.
replies.delivery: Use a clear, unhurried no; move toward your own exit if you want to leave.

replies.why: It declines completely in four words, with the good night doing the kindness.
replies.delivery: Use a clear, unhurried no; move toward your own exit if you want to leave.

replies.line: I don't move that fast — but I'd like a second date.
replies.why: It frames the no as your pace, not their failure, and offers the future explicitly.
replies.delivery: Use a clear, unhurried no; move toward your own exit if you want to leave.

replies.line: My place has a strict guest list. Me.
replies.why: The joke expresses that you are going home alone without insulting the invitation.
replies.delivery: Use a clear, unhurried no; move toward your own exit if you want to leave.

trap.line: Ugh, I knew this was all you wanted.
trap.why: It makes an assumption about their motives rather than simply stating your decision.

scenarios.goal: Decline intimacy at your own pace.

followUp.jab: Come on, don't you trust me?
followUp.line: Trust doesn't change my decision; I'm heading home on my own.
followUp.why: It keeps consent independent of a test of trust.
followUp.delivery: Use a clear, unhurried no; move toward your own exit if you want to leave.

scenarios.setting: On a first date, someone makes a joke at your expense that does not feel playful.

replies.line: That label doesn't work for me. Let's keep this respectful.
replies.why: It identifies the behavior you want changed without labeling the person.
replies.delivery: Pause, then say “That label doesn't work for me” at a steady, conversational volume. Avoid laughing to make the discomfort disappear.

replies.why: It makes a specific request rather than returning an insult.
replies.delivery: Say “Skip the labels, please” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. Avoid laughing to make the discomfort disappear.

replies.line: I like playful conversation; that comment didn't feel playful to me.
replies.why: It distinguishes welcome humor from the comment that crossed your boundary.
replies.delivery: Say “didn't feel playful” steadily; avoid laughing to make the discomfort disappear.

replies.line: My maintenance schedule doesn't include that joke.
replies.why: The joke sets a limit while directing the humor at the situation.
replies.delivery: Keep “My maintenance schedule doesn't include that joke” light; let the joke stand without repeating it. Avoid laughing to make the discomfort disappear.

followUp.line: I understand that was your intent; I'm still asking you not to repeat it.
followUp.why: It separates their intention from the boundary you are setting.
followUp.delivery: Pause before “I understand that was your intent,” keep the volume even, then allow an answer without reopening your decision.
